companyInfo.Industry: Health Care: Insurance and Managed Care

description: Centene is the largest Medicaid managed-care organization in the U.S. as of 2026. The company works with programs in the public and private sector to provide health care services to the underinsured and uninsured, military veterans, and commercial organizations. Programs it serves include Medicaid and Medicare plans, Medicare prescription drug plans, the Health Insurance Marketplace, and Tricare plans. It also operates its own health care and dental clinics and pharmacies.

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription:
The health care company, led by CEO Sarah London, focuses on insurance plans offered through Medicaid and the Affordable Care Act. Revenue was up 15% in 2022 from the previous year.

  • Centene’s $2.2 billion acquisition of behavioral-health specialist Magellan Health, completed in January 2022, was cited by the company as a major factor in its revenue growth for the year.

  • Elsewhere, Centene has been divesting itself of “noncore” subsidiaries in an ongoing review of its portfolio. Divisions that it has sold off include Magellan’s pharmacy and specialty-health units. In May 2023, Centene announced it would divest its A.I.-powered health care analytics company Apixio.

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription: A global health crisis continued to drive revenue growth at Centene, a health insurer with considerable exposure to the Medicaid and Affordable Care Act marketplaces. Revenue increased 13.4% in 2021, to $126 billion, and as of early 2022, Centene’s managed care membership had increased by 1.9 million over the previous year. In January 2022, Centene acquired Magellan Health for $2.2 billion, expanding its behavioral-health offerings. The company is also coping with a loss in the corner office: In April 2022, CEO Michael F. Neidorff, who headed Centene for more than 25 years, passed away after a long illness. Sarah London, formerly vice chairwoman, is now chief executive.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: A couple of strategic bets paid off for Centene over the past year. The health insurer dug in to the Affordable Care Act’s marketplaces even when the Obama-era health law’s future was far from certain, and through April 2021 it had added 320,000 new members under the Biden administration’s expanded special enrollment period for those individual insurance exchanges. Centene’s 2020 revenues exceeded $111 billion, after executives accurately predicted that the COVID pandemic would bring about a windfall, with growing demand for coronavirus-related services across the nation. The question is how long that win streak can last. “This a year with unique drivers,” said CEO Michael Neidorff in late April 2021, “which we cannot be certain can continue throughout all of 2022.”

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: Centene has at times been an oddity among its health insurance peers. In the past few years, the company has remained steadfast in serving the Affordable Care Act’s individual insurance markets, despite what would seem like never-ending legal and political uncertainty surrounding the government program. Well, it seems the skeptics lost that bet. Centene's strategy, coupled with acquisitions that focus on government-affiliated health plans like Medicare and Medicaid, propelled the insurer to 24% revenue growth in 2019, compared with the previous year. And it may benefit from another financial tailwind to come: The firm reportedly expects billions of dollars in revenue growth this year, due to the coronavirus crisis.

rankings.title: Change the World
rankings.itemDescription: This insurer’s 24 million members, the vast majority of whom belong to Medicaid, Medicare, and Health Insurance Marketplace plans, are disproportionately vulnerable to harm from the pandemic. Centene has leaned into the challenge of keeping them healthy by plowing money into infrastructure that helps Medicaid members access telehealth, and by removing barriers (like prior authorizations) to COVID-19 testing and care.
